basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 10.' and it opens '(Vers. 10.) Et congregationes aquarum vocavit maria. Notandum quod omnis congregatio'. The printing states no chapter here and the lemma is too short to match, so the chapter is the one the preceding block established.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 10.) Et congregationes aquarum vocavit maria. Notandum quod omnis congregatio aquarum, sive salsae sint, sive dulces, juxta idioma linguae Hebraicae, maria nuncupentur. Frustra igitur Porphyrius, Evangelistas ad faciendum ignorantibus miraculum, eo quod Dominus super mare ambulaverit, pro lacu Genezareth, mare appellasse calumniatur, cum omnis lacus et aquarum congregatio maria nuncupentur.
